Hi Anna — attaching the items requested via a secure share and including short answers inline. Links/attachments below.

Attachments (redacted for external sharing):
- Redwood_SOC2_Type_II_2025.pdf (redacted) — audit period: 2025-01-01 to 2025-12-31. Includes control testing for hosted services across regions; there are callouts when tests were specific to regional deployments.
- Redwood_DPA_v3_signed.pdf — includes incorporation of SCCs for transfers out of the EEA.
- SCCs_execution_statement.pdf — confirms Redwood has executed SCCs with our downstream subprocessors where they act as subprocessors of EU customer data. Note: SCCs with customers are executed via our standard DPA (clause referencing SCCs).
- subprocessors_list_2026.csv — identifies which subprocessors process EU data and which maintain EU‑only infrastructure.

Inline answers to your three follow ups:
1) Layering: Customers sign our DPA (which incorporates SCCs) with Redwood. We in turn require executed SCCs (or equivalent agreements) from our subprocessors when they process EU customer data. The SCCs_execution_statement provides the current status and effective dates.
2) SOC 2 regional samples: The 2025 SOC 2 testing included controls performed on our EU region deployments where applicable; the report includes notes where testing was region‑specific. We redacted internal IP but left the relevant testing scope statements intact in the share.
3) Logs & replication: Access logs may be collected in region and are retained according to the retention schedule in our DPA (outlined in the DPA attachment). For hosted accounts configured for EU‑only hosting, logs are stored in the EU and are encrypted at rest using customer‑segregated keys where requested (see subprocessors list for which partners support this). For default hosted accounts, some telemetry non‑PII metrics are aggregated globally; however, we do not replicate raw customer content outside the EEA for EU‑hosted accounts unless the customer explicitly enables cross‑region replication.
